_: The five findings of the lapis (Monitoring) hero, in the exact keys of findings-screening.json. Provenance: every figure in a/b/cote is a cell of ~/Documents/cascade-monitoring/releve-public.json at seal `sceau`; the builder refuses to build if the record on disk no longer matches. Each figure keeps its cell address in `source` ({table, palier, seuil, mesure} or {table, compte}); the optional `champ` names which field of the Rate is displayed when it is not `taux` (finding 03 displays lower bounds: champ = 'bas'). Builders may ignore `source`; reviewers and guards re-derive every number from it. The tool's rule behind finding 03 is the same as the whole suite: Wilson lower bound of recall at or above 0.90, then the fewest false alerts. Twin attributions in the phrases are measured, not assumed: at 0.50 the seven false alerts of `amount` are all one-off purchases, and `velocity` trips on payroll, seasonal trade and savings transfers. `annotations` are provisional fractions of the cascading-basins tray (anchor x, anchor y, label x, label y, text): the basins are not rendered yet, and the labels are to be reread against the rendered object before they ship.

findings.titre: The naked amount catches nearly everything.
findings.phrase: Score nothing but the biggest amount in the window and almost every archetype trips it. So does the family purchase the history explains: every one of its false alerts is the same benign twin, the one-off purchase.
findings.leg_a: recall of the amount scenario at 0.50, interval [84–99], 42 written suspicious cases
findings.leg_b: false alerts on the 42 benign twins, interval [8–31]: all of them one-off purchases
annotations: the first basin: one number, one spillway
the explained purchase spills with the suspects

findings.titre: A busy account is not a signal.
findings.phrase: Count transactions and payroll looks like laundering: the twins velocity trips on are the salary account, the market season and the monthly savings, while most true archetypes pass under it quietly.
findings.leg_a: recall of the velocity scenario at 0.50, interval [17–44]: most archetypes are not busy
findings.leg_b: false alerts at the same threshold, interval [36–64]: payroll, season and savings, measured
annotations: the counting basin overflows on payday

findings.titre: No single scenario holds the floor.
findings.phrase: The tool's rule asks the lower bound of measured recall to reach 90. On 42 written cases no cell of any scenario gets there alone: the best bound stops at 84, the next at 75. That is the honest headline, and the reason the sweep is worth running on your history.
findings.leg_a: the highest lower bound any single cell reaches: amount at 0.50, recall interval [84–99]
findings.leg_b: the next best bound: peer at 0.50, recall interval [75–95]
annotations: no spillway sits low enough on its own
what one basin misses, another must catch

findings.phrase: The same cell, two provenances. On generated variants the amount scenario scores a perfect recall; on the written cases it does not. Blended, the synthetic half would round the record's own doubt away. It is measured apart, labelled synthetic, and stays apart.
findings.leg_a: recall at amount 0.50 on the 42 written suspicious cases, interval [84–99]
findings.leg_b: the same cell on 126 generated variants, interval [97–100]: kept apart precisely because it flatters

findings.phrase: Every case behind these findings is ours: written twin by twin, or generated under a seed. Two files from your own systems, alerts and transactions, replay the whole grid on your machine. Nothing leaves it, and the report lands next to your files.
findings.leg_a: written suspicious cases behind the measured half, seven per declared nature
findings.leg_b: generated suspicious variants behind the synthetic half, natures preserved by construction
annotations: our basins end where your export begins
measure:yours, two files, at your desk
